Summary:

**What the source actually was:** The fixture page has zero CSS — no `<link>`, no `<style>`, no inline styles. Just two `<section>`s (`#hero`, `#specs`), each with a broken image reference and a paragraph of body copy. It renders in a plain browser with the native user-agent stylesheet: black-on-white, default paragraph margins, and native "broken image" icons (the `img` srcs are relative paths — `/founder.jpg`, `/spec-icon.svg` — that don't resolve to anything real).

**Key decision — no fabrication:** Since there's no color palette, typography, or layout anywhere in the source to reverse-engineer, I did not invent a "designed" hero section or specs grid (which would have been a plausible-but-fabricated restyle). I transcribed the copy verbatim ("Our founder started this company in a garage in 2011." / "Weighs 340 grams, shipped in recyclable packaging.") and kept the exact same two-section markup.

**Componentization:** None warranted — there's no repeated card/button pattern here, just two one-off content blocks, so I left them as plain semantic sections rather than inventing reusable component classes.

**Images:** Per the hotlinking rule I'd normally point at the live absolute URL, but this fixture has no real domain/host behind it — the paths are relative and unresolvable even on the "live" source. I kept the same relative references as-is so the clone reproduces the identical broken-image + alt-text behavior rather than guessing at a fake absolute URL.

**Tailwind setup:** Loaded the Tailwind CDN script per the required approach, but set `corePlugins.preflight = false` in the config — Tailwind's reset would have stripped the browser's default paragraph/image margins and changed the look, which would've actually hurt fidelity here since the "design" *is* the browser default stylesheet.

**JS-driven sections:** None present — no carousels, no lazy-loaded content, nothing to flag as unrecreatable.

**Screenshot comparison:** Took `original.png` and `clone-round1.png`, both at 1280×900. They came back byte-identical (21,293 bytes each) and visually identical on inspection — broken-image icons and text in the same positions. One round was sufficient; no further iteration was needed.
